# TurnVector

TurnVector coordinates multiple resident AI models sharing Apple Silicon. Its priorities are hard safety, interactive Decode latency isolation, weighted Engine Service fairness, and then throughput optimization.

## Language

**Turn**:
A bounded execution interval assigned to one Model. It ends only after execution is synchronized and persistent inference state is safe to continue. A logical Prefill may require many Turns, but each Prefill Turn advances exactly one Prefill Chunk before returning control.
_Avoid_: Request, token, Decode Step, Command Buffer

**Cooperative Turn Interleaving**:
The MVP execution-concurrency model in which a bounded number of requests for multiple Models may be live and Runnable while the Device Executor runs exactly one synchronized Turn at a time. Every accepted Turn Receipt returns control to the Runtime Core, and any continuation competes from a fresh Scheduling Snapshot and Turn Plan. It is the mechanism for request concurrency and bounded cross-Model latency isolation at certified yield points without claiming simultaneous Metal execution, command-buffer priority, or hard preemption.
_Avoid_: Concurrent Metal Turns, one request at a time, forced interruption

**Continuous Batching**:
Deterministic same-Model batch membership that may change only between synchronized Turns. Every execution still requires a fresh Scheduling Snapshot and Turn Plan; the term does not imply mid-Turn insertion, cross-Model batching, automatic continuation, or simultaneous Metal execution.
_Avoid_: Dynamic batching, Adapter scheduling loop, concurrent Metal Turns

**Scheduling Snapshot**:
An immutable statement of the runnable work, timing obligations, versioned cost estimates, execution capabilities, resource safety state, Monotonic Time, current Runtime Overhead Generation, daemon-associated exact applicable Runtime Overhead Bound Set identity for every Work Candidate, and complete Generation Vector available for one scheduling decision.
_Avoid_: Snapshot, mutable system state, queue length

**Work Candidate**:
A Model Planner-provided immutable description of one schedulable choice of compatible request handles for one Model, one Execution Phase, and one Service Class. Batch members cannot cross Service Classes. It carries an opaque Candidate ID, one exact Capability Key, and the timing, batching, output, and Resource Impact facts needed for selection without exposing tensors, KV layout, or backend shapes. Every member's frozen Authorized Capability Set must contain that exact Key, and Core can associate the Candidate only when every member has the same exact current Runtime Overhead Bound Set witness and Runtime Overhead Generation plus a live Future Turn Support Entitlement that can jointly fund the Plan's operation-scoped support obligations; the Backend neither selects nor composes that evidence. For Prefill, its execution and progress contract covers one next Prefill Chunk Turn, never the complete remaining prompt. It is infeasible if it cannot satisfy every member's current timing obligation, Progress Bound, or entitlement conservation check.
_Avoid_: Request queue, Tensor Batch

**Candidate Formation**:
The pure operation in which the Scheduler supplies eligible request handles and hard feasibility constraints, and the Model Planner returns a deterministic bounded set of immutable Work Candidates plus a Candidate Exclusion for every eligible request absent from those candidates. Its only typed causes are initial request progress, Receipt continuation, rejection disposition, local-stale disposition, and terminal membership change after cancellation removes a request from an existing candidate. Core represents one actual `form_candidates` invocation with one operation-scoped Support Operation Obligation funded by the canonical sorted set of one typed Support Funding Claim per affected request, regardless of member count: a request awaiting its first formation contributes its Admission-reserved initial claim, while later or membership-change formation contributes its entitlement-vector claim, and one mixed call may contain both variants without double funding. After the complete causal predecessor envelope has ended and immediately before preparation, one standalone Core `begin_support` transition converts that exact pending obligation and its single physical start credit; the Receipt, rejection, local-stale, cancellation, prior support Result, or newly eligible request transition may only mark it pending, atomically rebind or split/merge an unstarted obligation with exact conservation, or prove it impossible. A missing, wrong, duplicate, already closed, or prematurely converted obligation permits no call. Once active, its scope and funders are frozen through Result acceptance and retained-credit expiry. Each Candidate carries one complete exact Capability Key selected for that choice and is rejected unless every member's frozen Authorized Capability Set contains it and Core can associate one identical current Runtime Overhead Bound Set witness and Runtime Overhead Generation across all members. The Backend receives no applicability evidence and cannot merge or choose Sets. The MVP permits at most one candidate per Model ID, Execution Phase, Service Class, and configured batch bucket; Candidate Formation neither enumerates arbitrary request subsets nor consumes Model Weight, Model Ledger, cross-Model service debt, relative priority, or urgency order.
_Avoid_: Batch execution, Scheduler batching, backend queue

**Formation Result**:
The immutable bounded output of one Model-scoped Candidate Formation over an exact eligible-membership and Model-local dependency identity, containing complete Work Candidates and Candidate Exclusions. It records structural Backend choices but carries no current scheduling, Certification, resource, or fairness authority.
_Avoid_: Scheduling Snapshot, Turn Plan, authorization cache

**Candidate Association**:
The Runtime Core-owned current binding of one Formation Result to exact authorization, Runtime Overhead, resource, timing, Scheduler, and quarantine evidence. Only a current Candidate Association may contribute Candidates to a fresh Scheduling Snapshot, and replacing it never reuses a Turn Plan.
_Avoid_: Formation Result, cached Turn Plan, Backend authorization

**Model Planner**:
The private Execution Backend Module that owns same-Model structural execution feasibility, canonical Batch construction, KV and Shape compatibility, and Candidate Formation. It receives only eligible request facts and hard constraints, never Certification Applicability or Authorized Capability Sets, and cannot select which Model runs next or inspect global fairness policy.
_Avoid_: Turn Arbiter, cross-Model Scheduler, Adapter queue

**Batch Execution Kind**:
The stable graph-ABI discriminant that distinguishes a genuine multi-member tensor execution from a sequential per-member loop at the same configured batch and Shape bucket. It is part of Execution Route Identity, so one kind never inherits the other's Certification or telemetry label.
_Avoid_: Batch bucket, observed parallelism, throughput label

**Candidate Exclusion**:
A stable typed explanation for why one eligible request is absent from every Work Candidate produced in one Candidate Formation result. It is part of the bounded result and cannot be replaced by silent omission, free text, or a Backend priority decision.
_Avoid_: Admission rejection, request cancellation, hidden deferral

**Prefill Chunk**:
One contiguous resumable token-range advancement within a request's logical Prefill phase, executed as exactly one Prefill Turn. The Turn Plan supplies a target Engine Service, explicit work ceilings, and a certified hard execution bound; the Execution Backend uses its immutable Cost Profile plus current model, Batch, Shape, KV, and compile-cache state to choose the concrete token range. It evaluates and synchronizes the required output and persistent KV/cursor state before returning the processed range, continuation state, and yield reason in the Turn Receipt. A shared-mode implementation cannot loop over successive schedulable chunks or consume the remaining prompt before returning control.
_Avoid_: Full-prompt Turn, hidden chunk loop, Scheduler-selected Tensor shape

**Work Kind**:
An Execution Backend-defined category of model work that maps to TurnVector's fixed scheduling semantics. The Scheduler does not branch on Work Kind.
_Avoid_: Execution Phase, Service Class, Scheduler plugin

**Schedulable Work**:
Work whose exact Capability Key is authorized by a hash-bound Certification Record that supplies a certified execution bound, resumable Turn boundary, compatible Batch membership, output bound, Resource Impact, and conservative peak memory-delta upper bound. Work without those properties or outside the certified Envelope cannot enter shared scheduling.
_Avoid_: Arbitrary backend operation, loaded model

**Exclusive Mode**:
An explicit control-plane operating mode entered after the current Turn reaches a synchronized safe boundary and shared dispatch is paused. Accepted queues remain paused while one resource-bounded but otherwise unsupported non-yielding operation owns execution without cross-Model fairness, Interactive latency, Progress Bound, or total-duration guarantees; resource-safety rules remain in force. The operation must reach an Exclusive Safety Point within a certified interval, and work without a conservative peak resource bound is rejected even in this mode. Exit is an explicit control-plane action, and neither the Execution Backend nor the Resource Governor can enter it automatically.
_Avoid_: High priority, automatic fallback, ordinary Turn

**Exclusive Safety Point**:
A certified, periodically reachable boundary at which an Exclusive operation can stop or roll back without leaving backend state unsafe. Critical requests cancellation at the next such point; the interval is bounded even though total Exclusive Mode duration is not.
_Avoid_: Resumable Turn boundary, hard thread interruption

**Exclusive Lease**:
A renewable Control Plane lease required for an Exclusive operation to continue without a total-duration limit. Lease disconnect or expiry orders cancellation at the next Exclusive Safety Point; renewal cannot weaken Resource Mode restrictions.
_Avoid_: Fixed operation timeout, automatic Exclusive entry

**Turn Plan**:
Authorization for the fixed request membership of one Model and Work Candidate to consume one bounded Turn. It binds the Candidate's exact Capability Key and Shape bucket, target Engine Service, certified hard execution bound, exact Runtime Overhead Bound Set identity, Runtime Overhead Generation, intrinsic Stale Plan Disposition Bound identity and allowed successor ceiling, every member's Future Turn Support Entitlement identity, one Plan-scoped Receipt-observation obligation, one conditional continuation-Candidate-Formation obligation, and the mutually exclusive rejection/local-stale Candidate-Formation obligation atomically funded by all members before Plan creation, phase-specific work ceilings, and complete Generation Vector while leaving the concrete backend Shape representation, Prefill Chunk token count, and Decode burst choice within those frozen bounds to the Execution Backend. Each operation obligation carries exactly one physical start credit irrespective of Batch size and occupies one distinct outstanding-vector claim in every funding entitlement. Failure to conserve and lease every required obligation creates no Plan. Immediately before `execute_turn`, the Event Loop must match both the Generation Vector and Bound Set identity against current Core state and verify every entitlement and operation obligation; a mismatch produces a local Stale Turn Plan disposition through the separately qualified current intrinsic bound before Backend execution, not a Backend Plan Rejection or fabricated Turn result. It never authorizes an automatic same-Model continuation after the resulting Turn Receipt.
_Avoid_: Plan, execution graph, request

**Turn Receipt**:
The single synchronized outcome corresponding to a started Turn Plan. It records actual progress, including any processed Prefill token range and continuation, Engine Service, resumability, yield reason, and completed, cancelled, partial, or failed member outcomes so scheduling and recovery share one causal record. `still_runnable` is an observation, not permission to execute again without a fresh Scheduling Snapshot and Turn Plan. A Backend operation that cannot return a trustworthy synchronized result causes process-wide fail-stop and produces no fabricated indeterminate Turn Receipt.
_Avoid_: Receipt, success response, telemetry event

**Plan Rejection**:
The Backend non-execution result returned from `execute_turn` when a still-current Turn Plan fails a Backend-owned pre-execution Candidate, state, or bound validation before any route operation, including first-use compilation, starts. It consumes no Engine Service and produces no Turn Receipt; the Scheduler must take a new Scheduling Snapshot rather than substitute work. Beginning first-use compilation starts the Turn even when no MLX kernel has executed: compile failure is a typed started-Turn failure, compile-bound excess is a Bound Violation, and neither can be relabeled as Plan Rejection. A daemon-detectable Generation Vector or Runtime Overhead Bound Set mismatch is instead a local Stale Turn Plan disposition before the call and cannot fabricate this result.
_Avoid_: Failed Turn, retry Receipt

**Member Outcome**:
The per-request result within a Batch Turn Receipt. A failed member can be recovered independently only when the Execution Backend proves its persistent state was isolated; otherwise every member in the Batch becomes Quarantined Work.
_Avoid_: Batch-wide success flag, assumed isolation

**Output Publication**:
The successful enqueue of synchronized, staged output into the owning connection's already-reserved outbound capacity after the Scheduler accepts the Turn Receipt and atomically commits Request State. That enqueue is the publication point; a later socket-write failure causes Client Disconnect without retry or replay, and the Execution Backend never writes directly to a client channel.
_Avoid_: Token callback from Backend, output before Receipt

**Turn Output Reservation**:
The concrete output-channel capacity reserved immediately before an output-producing Turn for that Turn's maximum visible token count. The broader Resource Reservation budgets aggregate capacity but does not allocate the entire Max Output Tokens socket buffer up front. Without Turn Output Reservation, the candidate is temporarily non-runnable.
_Avoid_: Admission reservation, unbounded socket buffer, Device Executor blocking

**Token Request**:
The MVP Data Plane request expressed as input token IDs, one closed Generation Parameters value, required Service Class, a Model Alias or immutable Model Revision reference, Max Output Tokens, an optional presence-tracked caller Sampling Seed, and optional Stop Token Sequences. Before Request Acceptance the daemon validates revision-independent fields, resolves the selector exactly once, rejects an Unavailable target, validates Top K against the frozen Revision's registered Model Descriptor vocabulary size, validates context bounds, and fixes the effective Sampling Seed and origin. Tokenization, chat templates, text decoding, raw deadlines, and Backend-native generation objects belong outside TurnVector. Input length plus Max Output Tokens must not exceed the resolved Revision's context limit; TurnVector rejects overflow rather than truncating.
_Avoid_: Prompt request, chat message, backend-native object

**Generation Parameters**:
The immutable four-field P0 token-selection value containing required Sampling Mode, Temperature, Top P, and Top K. Mode is the closed mapping `UNSPECIFIED=0` invalid, `GREEDY=1`, and `CATEGORICAL=2`; Temperature and Top P retain their accepted IEEE-754 binary32 bit patterns, Top K is `u32`, and no field has a default. Omission, negative zero, NaN, or infinity is invalid. Greedy requires positive-zero Temperature, Top P exactly `1.0`, and Top K `0`. Categorical requires Temperature in `(0, 2]`, Top P in `(0, 1]`, and Top K either `0` for disabled or strictly below the registered Model Descriptor's nonzero vocabulary size. P0 has no configurable logits bias, repetition, presence, or frequency penalty, Min P, XTC, or opaque Backend parameter. The versioned schema identity and complete allowed domain bind Certification Applicability.
_Avoid_: Backend options map, model defaults, optional sampling fields

**Generation Semantics Identity**:
The immutable Evidence Hash of one canonical build-generated descriptor whose bytes enumerate the complete allowed Generation Parameters schema and domain, exact Greedy and Categorical token-selection algorithms, and Sampling RNG Schema transition. Deterministic double generation must reproduce the descriptor and hash. The same verified value is embedded in the daemon's Domain Type registry and in the Backend Bootstrap Manifest-bound complete Backend Capability descriptor; Backend Initialization requires exact equality before Service Readiness. The identity enters Environment Qualification, the fresh Environment Fingerprint, every applicable Certification Envelope, and the Admission cache key, so schema, domain, token-selection, or RNG drift fails closed rather than inheriting authorization.
_Avoid_: Adapter self-attestation, model sampling defaults, runtime-inferred algorithm

**Max Output Tokens**:
The required per-request upper bound on generated tokens. Admission uses it to bound KV growth and output capacity; an unbounded generation request is invalid.
_Avoid_: Global default only, soft stopping hint

**Output Sequence**:
The monotonic per-request token position assigned only to visible published output. An Output Frame carries the first Output Sequence plus a contiguous token-ID vector, which determines every sequence in that frame. Delivery is ordered and at most once within the live owning Data Plane connection; disconnect causes Cooperative Cancellation and no output is replayed after reconnect.
_Avoid_: Durable stream offset, frame ID, exactly-once delivery

**Output Frame**:
The single bounded output unit that one committed Turn may produce for one request. It contains zero or more contiguous visible token IDs, their starting Output Sequence, the resulting Request Status Version, and optional terminal reason, but never substitutes for the independent terminal Status Update. When one transition produces both, the Output Frame is published first; the MVP has no frame acknowledgement or retransmission.
_Avoid_: Per-token IPC request, full-request buffer, Audit Journal record

**Sampling State**:
The per-request Generation Parameters, effective Sampling Seed, and current Sampling RNG Schema state owned and executed by the in-process C++/MLX Adapter on the Device Executor alongside KV state. Categorical selection consumes exactly one request draw key and commits exactly one next state for every sampled token, including a token hidden or withheld by Stop Token Sequences; Greedy neither draws nor advances the state. The Adapter returns token IDs rather than logits or RNG state to Core or the caller.
_Avoid_: Daemon sampling, client logits stream

**Sampling Seed**:
The immutable effective per-request `u64` fixed before Request Acceptance together with origin `caller` or `daemon`. Caller presence is explicit and every value, including zero, is valid. If absent, the daemon reads exactly eight bytes from macOS `SecRandomCopyBytes`, interprets them as little-endian `u64`, supplies the result to Core before Acceptance, exposes it and its origin in the Acceptance response, and emits both in the ordered Audit Effect. CSPRNG failure rejects before Acceptance and never falls back to time, a constant, or process-global RNG.
_Avoid_: Per-Turn seed, Adapter-global RNG, treating absence as zero

**Sampling RNG Schema**:
The versioned per-request state transition that initializes `mlx::core::random::key(seed)` as pinned-build `uint32[2] {high32, low32}` and, for each Categorical token, calls `split(state)`, persists the first result as the next state, and supplies the second as the sole `random::categorical` draw key. Greedy performs no split. Its identity and exact multi-token vectors enter the Certification Envelope; Batch membership, member order, Turn boundaries, hidden stop tokens, and process-global state cannot alter the transition.
_Avoid_: Shared batch RNG, reseeding each Turn, unspecified MLX random state

**Categorical Token Selection**:
The exact pinned-MLX binary32 algorithm applied after every model logit and its binary32 cast are proven finite. It computes `centered = logits - max(logits)`, `weights = exp(centered)`, `normalizer = sum(weights)`, `log_probabilities = centered - log(normalizer)`, then separately `probabilities = exp(log_probabilities)`. Top P `1.0` retains all entries; otherwise ascending `(log_probability, token_id)` order, inclusive binary32 cumulative probability, and an inclusive `cumulative <= 1 - Top P` mask discard the low tail, retaining the first strict crossing and all later entries. No crossing retains only the greatest log probability with lower token ID winning. Top K then keeps the greatest `min(Top K, surviving_count)` entries, with lower token ID winning ties, unless zero disables it. Retained `(token_id, log_probability)` pairs are compacted in ascending token-ID order, shifted by their maximum, divided by Temperature, sampled only within that nonempty compact vector, and mapped back to token ID. It never substitutes `weights / normalizer`, exposes masked entries to `random::categorical`, or applies Temperature before Top P and Top K.
_Avoid_: Backend-default sampler, full-vocabulary masked categorical, approximate softmax

**Stop Token Sequences**:
The optional bounded token-ID sequences evaluated by the in-process C++/MLX Adapter alongside Max Output Tokens. The Adapter retains the longest suffix that might still form a stop sequence and publishes only tokens proven not to belong to one; matched stop tokens are not visible by default. The terminating Turn Receipt records whether completion came from a stop sequence, output limit, cancellation, or failure.
_Avoid_: Text stop string, daemon-side late cancellation

**Batch-Invariant Sampling**:
The requirement that one request produce the same token and Sampling RNG state vectors for the same Model Revision, input token IDs, exact Generation Parameters bit patterns, effective Sampling Seed, Max Output Tokens, Stop Token Sequences, and generated-token/state prefix regardless of Batch membership, member order, other requests, or Turn interleaving. Stop-token visibility may withhold output but cannot undo or defer the sampled token's Categorical state advance.
_Avoid_: Adapter-global RNG, batch-dependent output

**Model**:
The stable Model ID that receives one configured weight and competes with other runnable Models for Engine Service. Every Model Revision registered under that ID shares the same Model Weight and Model Ledger; a revision change cannot create additional fair share.
_Avoid_: Tenant, user, request

**Runnable Model**:
A Model with at least one currently valid Work Candidate. Only Runnable Models participate in Engine Service fairness, and idle time creates no service credit for future work.
_Avoid_: Loaded Model, active process

**Model Weight**:
The configured relative share of Engine Service owed to a Runnable Model over a sufficiently long steady-state interval. It is not a strict short-window guarantee and cannot override resource safety.
_Avoid_: Priority, request weight

**Weight Change**:
An atomic Model Weight update applied only at a Turn boundary. The affected Model Ledger is aligned to the current runnable baseline, so the new weight changes only future service rate and creates neither historical debt nor stored credit.
_Avoid_: Ledger reset, historical rescaling

**Model Ledger**:
The single weighted virtual-service account shared by every Work Kind, Model Revision, and request belonging to one Model ID. Each Turn adds its actual Engine Service divided by Model Weight; normal fair selection chooses the Runnable Model with the smallest account after runnable-baseline alignment.
_Avoid_: Work Kind quota, request ledger

**Engine Service**:
The Device Executor-measured Monotonic Time from beginning direct execution of a valid Turn Plan until that Turn's C++/MLX work is synchronized. It includes graph build, submission, and wait time, but excludes ingress queueing, pre-execution Scheduler selection, Receipt commit, and output-consumer time. Only this duration advances the Model Ledger; no process-boundary clock mapping or internal transport time exists. This is the synchronized engine-service basis permitted by the P-1A YELLOW result, not MLX command-buffer service time or GPU occupancy.
_Avoid_: Token count, queue time, GPU occupancy

**TurnVector Daemon Build Identity**:
The Daemon Core Build Identity includes the Catalog schema, fixed maximum entry and byte counts, lookup/matching algorithm, executable and native text-section identities, and the worst-case work bound for a maximum-size Catalog. The generated payload occupies a deterministic non-executable read-only section whose bytes cannot alter those code identities; changing payload bytes changes Catalog and outer identities, while changing its schema, capacity, algorithm, or executable layout changes the Core identity. This structural split is what permits external lifecycle evidence to bind the Core identity without certifying a self-referential final binary.
The exact Evidence Hash of a canonical two-level build descriptor. Its Daemon Core Build Identity binds an exact path-and-content-hashed runtime source-closure manifest, compiler and dependency locks, feature/profile set, protocol and domain registries, native Interface and Adapter inputs, and every executable semantic input except the generated Runtime Overhead Catalog payload. Repository files outside that declared closure cannot silently affect the daemon artifact; adding a real build input without adding it to the closure fails dependency tracing. Each catalog entry binds that Core identity; the separate Catalog Identity hashes the complete canonical catalog; and the outer Daemon Build Identity hashes both identities. Build verification checks the embedded tuple and final binary provenance, so neither a catalog entry nor the catalog hash recursively contains the outer identity and any runtime code, tool, dependency, registry, native, or catalog change produces a different exact build identity.
_Avoid_: Final-binary self hash, source commit alone, mutable build label

**Runtime Overhead Catalog**:
The compiler rejects payloads beyond the Core-build-fixed entry or byte maximum, and qualification covers worst-case lookup and matching at those maxima rather than assuming the actual embedded payload is free.
The finite build-generated read-only collection of every Owner-Thread Support Budget, Sequenced Event Interference Bound, and companion Stale Plan Disposition Bound that this daemon may activate. One canonical schema, deterministic compiler, checked lock, and Catalog Identity bind each entry's Daemon Core Build Identity, complete Configuration Snapshot identity, stable platform Envelope, expected Backend Bootstrap Manifest and returned descriptor identities, span/lifecycle schema, complete Lifecycle Evidence Table identities, positive sliding horizons, nonborrowable pools, and exhaustive twelve-operation, sequenced-event, and local-stale classifications. The compiler derives one Catalog Retention Horizon equal to the largest support horizon in any production entry and proves joint fixed active-charge, physical-credit, typed ordinary-reservation-claim, unstarted `conditional`- and `pending`-operation-obligation, Future Turn Support Entitlement vector/tombstone, post-load/post-observation description-reserve, first/next safety-reserve, and one dedicated Prepared Carry record capacity over the finite unbatched request closure, Model Registry Limit, and global/per-connection Ingress Budget bounds on Warming and active requests for every allowed activation sequence. That nonborrowable carry capacity also includes the maximum dual-Budget mandatory-completion and safety-sampling suballocation; a full ordinary ledger cannot consume it, and an entry cannot introduce a longer runtime horizon. Lifecycle Evidence Tables bind the Daemon Core Build Identity, never the outer TurnVector Daemon Build Identity or request Certification Case Bound Tables; this preserves the two-level build graph. Catalog entries reference only immutable external Lifecycle Evidence Table identities and provenance rather than copying large runs. Lifecycle Overhead Qualification is a later derived witness over one entry, those tables, current stable platform facts, and returned Backend descriptors; it is never an input to Catalog generation. Missing, duplicate, unknown, noncanonical, unqualified, or unclassified entries fail generation or startup; runtime code cannot add, infer, or widen an entry.
Every entry additionally carries a finite per-operation and per-pool Support Start Count Bound for every configured half-open horizon. The compiler proves active-record and typed start-credit capacity over the maximum legal sequential request/support churn, every activation sequence, and maximum accepted-request cardinality; concurrency alone is not a sufficient capacity proof.
_Avoid_: Runtime estimator, Certification Authorization Index, Backend-provided catalog

**Lifecycle Evidence Table**:
An immutable external table of exact lifecycle-operation, sequenced Core-event, or local-stale daemon-envelope bounds used only by Runtime Overhead Catalog generation and Lifecycle Overhead Qualification. Its identity binds the Daemon Core Build Identity and never carries a request Capability Key, Certification Record, or request Case Bound Table. The three table kinds remain separately typed; this umbrella term does not permit one kind to substitute for another.
_Avoid_: Case Bound Table, request certification evidence, runtime observation

**Catalog Retention Horizon**:
The build-derived maximum positive support sliding horizon across every production Runtime Overhead Catalog entry that the process can activate. The Catalog compiler uses it with every Support Start Count Bound, operation-obligation and physical-credit maximum, accepted-request entitlement-vector/tombstone cardinality, lifecycle-reserve maximum, and dedicated Prepared Carry plus dual-Budget suballocation maximum to prove fixed Support Charge Ledger capacity under maximum consecutive-Turn and sequential churn. Core retains every active charge, consumed start credit, and linked entitlement claim until this horizon can no longer reference it, regardless of the currently active Budget, so a later short-to-long Configuration successor cannot reset history. Runtime configuration cannot extend it.
_Avoid_: Current Budget horizon, dynamic retention knob, observed call lifetime

**Support Start Count Bound**:
A finite build-generated checked maximum number of support-envelope starts for one typed operation and nonborrowable pool in each configured Monotonic half-open window `[t, t + H)`. Every Support Operation Obligation owns exactly one physical start credit irrespective of request-member count, and the sole Core `begin_support` transition moves that credit into its active record rather than creating another claim. Optional ordinary work must acquire a currently legal credit in that same transition; exhaustion defers or rejects before preparation or Effect issuance. Admission-reserved request vectors and lifecycle mandatory-completion and safety-sampling pools are separately pre-reserved and cannot be borrowed by ordinary work. A consumed credit returns only after the Catalog Retention Horizon can no longer place its start in any applicable window. The Catalog compiler proves capacity across exact-window and one-past boundaries, maximum unbatched and shared-operation demand, sequential churn, and every allowed Configuration activation sequence; runtime observation cannot infer, replenish, or widen the bound.
_Avoid_: Observed request rate, concurrency-only limit, refundable call counter

**Support Outstanding Credit Vector**:
The finite request-specific map from `{support operation, nonborrowable pool, configured horizon}` to the maximum number of simultaneous conditional, pending, active, or retained claims reserved by one Future Turn Support Entitlement. Admission derives it conservatively from the finite Token Request closure, including Prefill Chunk count, maximum output tokens, all authorized result branches, the unbatched worst case, and Catalog count bounds, then atomically reserves the complete vector and its unbatched physical-credit backing against later Admission. One operation-scoped obligation funded by multiple requests occupies one vector slot in every funding entitlement but materializes only one physical start credit and one global start count. The other funders' split headroom remains attached to their vectors: a pre-start split may materialize the separately backed credits, while a merge returns surplus only to those same entitlement claims and never to unreserved global capacity. A claim remains occupied from obligation creation while conditional or pending; typed causal impossibility before start returns it only to the same entitlement slot, while `begin_support` binds it through active execution and retained-credit expiry. A terminal request leaves a bounded retained entitlement tombstone until every linked conditional, pending, active, or retained claim closes. Thus consecutive started Turns in one Catalog horizon consume distinct vector slots, while expiry returns a slot to the same entitlement rather than to unreserved global headroom. Catalog generation proves the summed vectors plus pre-Admission description and safety lifecycle pools fit fixed ledger storage and every Support Start Count Bound under the maximum accepted-request, bounded Warming/Preparing, and Model Registry cardinalities.
_Avoid_: One reusable token, concurrency count, unreserved global headroom

**Lifecycle Overhead Qualification**:
Its immutable external Lifecycle Evidence Tables bind the Daemon Core Build Identity rather than the outer daemon identity; request Certification Case Bound Tables are a separate Admission input and never feed the Catalog.
Immutable external evidence that one exact Runtime Overhead Catalog entry bounds daemon lifecycle, sequenced Core-event interference, and local stale-disposition work in one stable platform and implementation Envelope. Before Backend Initialization, the daemon collects the required device, GPU, unified-memory, macOS, Daemon Core Build, Configuration, Catalog, Bootstrap Manifest, and expected descriptor facts. After Initialization returns, a daemon-owned pre-activation matcher completes the startup qualification by comparing the returned Adapter, MLX, Interface, Capability, Resource Signal, and Operation Bound identities before any support call. Before a later Configuration successor can enter durable publication, the same matcher is the sole selector of its exact Catalog entry and must qualify it against the unchanged returned descriptors and fresh stable platform facts; absence or drift rejects that proposal before publication. The matcher returns one immutable qualification witness binding the proposed Configuration identity, selected Catalog entry and three lifecycle descriptor identities, stable facts, returned descriptor identities, and witness generation. Core never evaluates those external facts or selects a descriptor: it checks the supplied witness identity/current generation, prepares carry, and may atomically activate only that exact witness after committed Control publication. Qualification grants only activation of that entry's Owner-Thread Support Budget, Sequenced Event Interference Bound, and Stale Plan Disposition Bound; it is not Certification Applicability, never enters the Admission cache, and cannot authorize a request or Capability Key. Resource Evidence freshness is deliberately not an input, so the already qualified safety-sampling path can establish or restore that evidence; stable platform or implementation identity drift invalidates the qualification and fails closed.
The activated Owner-Thread Support Budget includes the entry's exact Support Start Count Bounds and start-credit capacities; qualification cannot select the time bounds while omitting their finite-start proof.
_Avoid_: Request certification, Backend self-attestation, Resource Evidence sample

**Runtime Overhead**:
The daemon-owned Monotonic Time outside Engine Service needed to form and select a Plan, validate in-memory Backend results, commit Runtime Core state, publish staged output, and execute bounded owner-thread support or sequenced Core-event work. One Turn-attempt partition begins with the first not-yet-accounted daemon work used to select or form that attempt's Plan. On a Receipt branch it ends after the accepted Receipt transition and every directly resulting Output Publication enqueue; on a Plan Rejection or local pre-dispatch Stale Turn Plan branch it ends after the Domain Rejection transition and one intrinsic fresh-Snapshot/replanning disposition. That intrinsic disposition ends before any `form_candidates` preparation: Candidate Formation is always a separate Owner-Thread Support envelope and is represented once by support interference. If the disposition selects a replacement candidate, the replacement Turn partition begins after any separately measured Candidate Formation and cannot measure the same intrinsic Snapshot or selection interval again. The complete `execute_turn` direct-call interval is measured once and classified only from its typed result: Receipt makes the whole interval Engine Service, while Backend Plan Rejection makes the whole interval Runtime Overhead. A local stale disposition performs no Backend call and uses its separately active qualified Stale Plan Disposition Bound, whose value was admitted beneath the rejection envelope ceiling; it never treats the stale Set as evidence or creates a third unbounded branch. Each owner-thread support operation has a separate complete daemon envelope beginning with either its optional reservation or, after any causal predecessor envelope ends, its standalone `begin_support` transition, and continuing through preparation, direct call, result translation and validation, accepted Core transition, and immediate in-memory Effect issuance; its Backend direct-call interval remains an independently bounded watchdog subspan. Every other Core Event allowed to pass a scheduling cut has a separate complete Sequenced Event envelope. Turn-attempt, support, and sequenced-event envelopes are ordered, disjoint, and complete, so no interval is omitted, overlapped, or charged twice. Runtime Overhead is bounded for timing feasibility and never charged to a Model Ledger.
_Avoid_: Engine Service, client queue time, free deadline time

**Runtime Overhead Bound Set**:
A measured Turn-envelope excess is also a certified Bound Violation: Core preserves any trustworthy Receipt, quarantines the most specific affected Capability Key through the existing violation transition, then advances Runtime Overhead Generation once through the non-Control evidence-invalidation owner before further dispatch. Generation invalidation never replaces or weakens quarantine.
The finite immutable daemon-owned descriptor that supplies conservative Runtime Overhead bounds for timing feasibility. Its typed identity binds the span-schema version, exact TurnVector Daemon Build Identity, complete Configuration Snapshot identity, Hot-Path Work Budget identity and maxima, one fresh Environment Fingerprint, the exact finite Certification Applicability Selection and all selected Certification Record and Case Bound Table identities, Backend Operation Bound Set identity, complete finite Turn-result case table, exact active Owner-Thread Support Budget identity plus sliding-horizon table, active Sequenced Event Interference Bound identity and table, and active Stale Plan Disposition Bound identity and value. The pure Admission calculation deterministically constructs it only from the immutable selection Admission owns and the already active qualified lifecycle descriptors; Core may commit it only together with the exact accepted Authorized Capability Set, Timing Commitment, actual initial-Materialization, initial-Candidate-Formation, and pre-materialization-release Support Operation Obligations, reusable Future Turn Support Entitlement with its complete Support Outstanding Credit Vector, finite per-Turn and terminal membership-change operation requirements, and composite Resource Reservation. Runtime instrumentation may enforce and measure the Core-supplied Set but cannot derive applicability or construct an authoritative Set. It is derived runtime evidence, not persisted Control State, a Backend result, Cost Profile state, or an online estimator. It contains disjoint upper bounds for pre-call intrinsic work, Receipt post-call work, and the Plan Rejection direct call plus rejection handling and one intrinsic fresh-Snapshot/replanning disposition; it references, rather than creates, every complete support-operation daemon-envelope bound, `support_interference(H)` entry, and `sequenced_event_interference(H)` entry in the lifecycle budget. Initial, continuation, rejection-driven, local-stale, and cancellation membership-change Candidate Formation remain separate support envelopes begun only by the post-predecessor standalone `begin_support` transition. Any missing entry, identity drift, Turn-envelope measured excess, or changed span schema makes the Set inapplicable, advances Runtime Overhead Generation before further dispatch, blocks unsafe new Timing Commitments, invalidates older not-started Scheduling Snapshots and Turn Plans, and triggers Profile Revalidation for dependent commitments. A measured Owner-Thread Support, Sequenced Event, or local-stale envelope excess instead invalidates Lifecycle Overhead Qualification and invokes process-wide fail-stop before another Backend or scheduling call. Online observations may diagnose or invalidate evidence but never create or widen it.
The exact active Owner-Thread Support Budget identity includes its Support Start Count Bound table. Admission reserves actual initial obligations' typed start credits plus each Future Turn Support Entitlement's complete Support Outstanding Credit Vector together with the support capacity represented by the Set; it does not pre-create every future Turn obligation. Each actual shared support call is later represented once by one operation-scoped obligation.
_Avoid_: Backend Operation Bound Set, observed average latency, dynamic safety margin

**Owner-Thread Support Budget**:
The finite immutable preverified daemon-owned lifecycle descriptor that limits all seven non-Turn, non-Residency, non-Exclusive Backend Interface operations from successful Backend Initialization until immediately before Backend Shutdown: `describe_model`, `describe_request`, `materialize_request`, `release_request`, `form_candidates`, `observe_turn_receipt`, and `sample_backend_resources`. Before initialization, the daemon selects exactly one candidate entry from the embedded Runtime Overhead Catalog by exact Daemon Core Build, complete active Configuration Snapshot, stable platform facts, span/lifecycle schema, horizons, pools, and expected Backend descriptor identities. If no exact entry exists, startup fails rather than synthesizing a budget online. Successful initialization activates the selected descriptor only after the pre-activation matcher completes its Lifecycle Overhead Qualification against every returned descriptor; therefore bootstrap description and the first safety sample needed to establish Resource Evidence are qualified and bounded before Service Readiness or any Admission exists. For a later Configuration successor, the matcher is the sole selector and must return the exact immutable qualified replacement witness before publication; Core only verifies identity/current generation and activates that witness. It is not constructed by Admission or returned by the Backend. Its closed lifecycle matrix permits only bootstrap description and safety sampling before readiness; all seven while ready; only already-required Receipt observation, release, description revalidation, and safety sampling while evidence is degraded or recovering; and only already-required Receipt observation, release, and safety sampling while draining. No new materialization or Candidate Formation occurs outside readiness. For every operation and bounded input bucket, the budget combines the externally verified direct-call bound with a certified complete daemon-envelope bound from a typed Ordinary Reservation Claim, obligation, credit, and active-record creation transition or a standalone pending-obligation `begin_support` transition, after any causal predecessor envelope has ended, through preparation and immediate in-memory Effects. The direct call has an independent watchdog, while Admission binds this exact active identity and interference table into each Runtime Overhead Bound Set. Any watchdog or complete-envelope excess invalidates Lifecycle Overhead Qualification and triggers process-wide fail-stop before another Backend operation; observation can never widen the Catalog entry.
The descriptor also binds the finite per-operation/pool Support Start Count Bound table and fixed typed start-credit capacities used by the sole Core Support Charge Ledger.
Description revalidation and safety sampling are never post-trigger allocations. Before a Residency load may start, the sole Core Support Charge Ledger owner reserves a bounded post-load Model/Request-description obligation set from the mandatory-completion pool; load failure or cancellation closes it, while successful load makes the exact set pending for the sole description owner. Before Receipt observation may start, its distinct operation obligation already carries the bounded post-update description-revalidation set that its Result must mark pending or close. Lifecycle Overhead Qualification activates a first Resource-sample obligation before Service Readiness, and the sole safety trigger maintains the next nonborrowable safety obligation before current Resource Evidence can expire. These lifecycle-scoped obligations use the same ledger, count bounds, pending/`begin_support`/typed-impossibility rules, and complete envelopes as request-funded obligations.

For each configured positive Monotonic Time horizon `H`, `support_interference(H)` is the certified checked maximum sum of active charges and all unstarted operation-scoped obligations, whether `conditional` or `pending`, whose complete envelopes can occupy the owner thread in any half-open interval `[t, t + H)`, independent of clock alignment. It includes ordinary, mandatory-completion, and safety-sampling pools; mandatory completion covers initial Request Materialization and Candidate Formation, accepted-Receipt observation plus any required continuation Candidate Formation, rejection- or local-stale-driven Candidate Formation, cancellation membership-change Candidate Formation, post-load or post-observation description revalidation, and ownership-gated release. It counts a carry-in envelope started before `t` and still active at `t`, counts a crossing envelope once at its full reserved bound, and includes carry-out without granting a second adjacent-window charge. For a truly optional ordinary invocation, one typed Ordinary Reservation Claim, one operation obligation, and one credit are atomically acquired in the typed Core reservation transition and the Backend call may begin only after Core commits its active charge. Successful Admission instead obtains actual initial-Materialization, initial-Candidate-Formation, and release obligations and creates one reusable Future Turn Support Entitlement with its complete outstanding-credit vector before its Timing Commitment exists. Before each Turn starts, Core atomically creates one Receipt-observation obligation, one conditional continuation-formation obligation, and the mutually exclusive rejection/local-stale formation obligation; every obligation is funded by every Plan member and carries its own single physical credit regardless of member count. The entitlement separately funds one terminal membership-change formation obligation only when removal invalidates candidate membership. Failure creates no Plan or cancellation transition. A Receipt, rejection, local-stale, cancellation, or support Result may mark its successor obligation pending, atomically rebind an unstarted scope, or prove the causal operation impossible but cannot start the successor envelope. Only after that complete predecessor envelope ends and immediately before preparation does one standalone Core `begin_support` transition convert the exact pending obligation to one active absolute-time charge. Receipt Output Publication enqueue or discard must therefore finish before observation conversion. Materialization failure closes the now-impossible initial-formation obligation, while an accepted Receipt retains the distinct continuation obligation as conditional until the observation Result proves formation required or impossible. Safety capacity and the next sample obligation likewise exist before a sample becomes required. Ordinary calls cannot borrow those pools, and nonessential work defers or rejects before invocation if every applicable sliding-horizon or start-count constraint cannot remain satisfied. A Deadline Cost selects one certified horizon covering its complete branch plus `support_interference(H)` and `sequenced_event_interference(H)`; no suitable entry rejects the candidate, and each interference term is added exactly once rather than hidden in intrinsic Turn spans. A noncancellable call's safe point is its bounded direct-call return.

**Contingent Mandatory Support Reservation**:
A bounded Core-owned prospective claim on one nonborrowable support pool for a causal call that may become mandatory later. Admission obtains separate initial-Materialization, initial-Candidate-Formation, and ownership-release obligations. Turn creation leases separate Plan-scoped Receipt-observation and conditional continuation-formation obligations plus the mutually exclusive rejection/local-stale Candidate-Formation alternative from every member's Future Turn Support Entitlement; that entitlement also funds terminal membership-change formation when cancellation changes a candidate. The release obligation does not pay for Materialization; it guarantees the later ownership-consuming release path if Materialization creates state. Every obligation reduces applicable sliding-horizon headroom, owns one typed start credit, and has no Monotonic start until conversion. A continuation obligation starts in the formal `conditional` unstarted state at Plan creation, retains its credit, claims, vector slots, storage and every applicable-horizon charge, and only its observation Result may move it to `pending` or typed-impossible close it. Any causal predecessor transition may otherwise mark its successor pending, atomically rebind an unstarted scope with exact conservation, or close it on typed impossibility. After that complete predecessor envelope ends and immediately before preparation, one standalone Core `begin_support` transition atomically converts the exact pending obligation into one active Support Charge Ledger entry. Configuration carry preserves it exactly.
_Avoid_: Active timed charge, Event Loop flag, refundable completed work

**Support Funding Claim**:
The fixed-capacity Core ledger claim by which one request, lifecycle trigger, or exact optional ordinary reservation contributes conserved capacity to one Support Operation Obligation. Its closed variants are an Admission-reserved actual initial-Materialization, initial-Candidate-Formation, or ownership-release claim; one slot in a Future Turn Support Entitlement's Support Outstanding Credit Vector; one typed description/safety lifecycle-reserve claim; or one typed Ordinary Reservation Claim created only by the sole Core optional-reservation transition for one exact operation, pool, input bucket, and ledger generation. A request-scoped operation has exactly one applicable claim per affected request, a lifecycle operation has exactly one trigger claim, and an optional ordinary operation has exactly one Ordinary Reservation Claim with no request or lifecycle sponsor; a mixed Candidate Formation may combine initial and entitlement variants. Claims reserve unbatched split headroom but do not multiply a shared operation's single physical start credit. They may move among unstarted split/merge/rebind results with exact conservation, never sponsor another request, and remain linked to active/retained records until their typed expiry.
_Avoid_: Physical start credit, sponsor request, Backend capacity grant

**Support Operation Obligation**:
The sole Core-owned operation-scoped authorization for exactly one future invocation of one Owner-Thread Support Backend operation. It binds a stable obligation identity, operation and pool, bounded input bucket, causal predecessor, exact call scope, one physical start credit, and a canonical sorted nonempty set of typed Support Funding Claims. Its closed unstarted states are `conditional`, while the causal predicate is unresolved, and `pending`, after the call is proven required and its predecessor is complete; only `pending` may enter `begin_support`. A shared Batch/Model call still has one obligation, one start credit, and one envelope; each affected request contributes exactly one applicable claim, so member count never multiplies the physical start count. An optional ordinary call instead carries exactly one Ordinary Reservation Claim created atomically with that obligation, credit, and active record. Before `begin_support`, Core may atomically rebind, split, merge, or close obligations after any bounded eligibility or candidate-membership change only when physical-credit backing, every funding claim, call scope, and causal conservation all remain exact; newly eligible members must join funding before they enter the call scope, and no member can sponsor another. After `begin_support`, scope and funders are frozen through accepted Result and Catalog-horizon retention; terminal entitlement funders remain as bounded tombstones until their linked claims expire. Description revalidation is funded before a load or observation can make it mandatory, and safety sampling is funded by the qualification-activated nonborrowable safety schedule before freshness can expire. No Backend Effect, Event Loop path, Result transition, or individual request sponsors or converts an obligation.
_Avoid_: Per-member Backend call, sponsor request, Event Loop token, post-trigger allocation

**Support Charge Ledger**:
Every durable Control successor uses the carry protocol below. References to a replacement Configuration describe the changed-Configuration case; when Configuration is unchanged, predecessor and successor Budget identities are exactly equal and the currently qualified lifecycle descriptors remain active.
The sole Runtime Core-owned bounded ledger of active support-envelope charges and unstarted Support Operation Obligations in `conditional` or `pending` state, reusable request-lifetime Future Turn Support Entitlements with finite Support Outstanding Credit Vectors, typed ordinary-reservation claims, typed lifecycle-trigger reserves, and one dedicated Prepared Carry slot. Every active charge binds an obligation identity, active Budget identity, nonborrowable pool, frozen call scope and canonical funding-claim set, absolute Monotonic start, one physical start credit, and full certified envelope bound; typed optional-reservation acceptance or standalone `begin_support` conversion starts that envelope immediately, so unrelated work or delay after that point consumes the same bound and any overrun follows the qualification fail-stop path. Every unstarted obligation binds its causal predecessor, exact request-funded or lifecycle-trigger funding, operation, full prospective bound, pool, input bucket, one credit, and exact conditional-to-pending/rebind/convert/impossible-close transitions without starting a timer. Every entitlement binds one Timing Commitment, complete finite request closure, outstanding-credit vector, exact Budget and Bound Set identities, and its allowed operation-funding transitions; it is created with Admission, remains conserved across consecutive Turns, and becomes a bounded terminal tombstone while any linked claim is retained. No predecessor Result transition may convert its successor obligation: only a later standalone `begin_support` transition after the complete predecessor envelope ends can do so. The Event Loop neither stores nor mutates any record kind, and a shorter observation never refunds an active charge. The build-derived Catalog Retention Horizon, not the currently active Budget's largest horizon, controls active-record and linked-claim expiration, so a later qualified successor with a longer horizon can still account for every charge it may reference. Unstarted obligations remain through any `conditional`-to-`pending` transition until exact conversion or typed causal impossibility. A monotonically increasing Support Ledger Generation identifies the exact charge, obligation, entitlement, ordinary claim, lifecycle reserve, and carry state.
The ledger also owns the fixed typed physical start-credit pool derived from every active Catalog entry's Support Start Count Bounds. Each unstarted operation obligation and retained active record consumes one credit; each request funder separately consumes one typed initial or entitlement-vector claim, while each optional ordinary record consumes its sole Ordinary Reservation Claim. `begin_support` is the sole transition whose optional branch atomically creates one typed Ordinary Reservation Claim, matching one-operation obligation, currently legal credit, and active record, or whose pending branch moves one existing obligation's credit to its active record. Typed causal impossibility may close an unstarted obligation and return its claims only to their original reserves; after start, the record, credit, and funder claims remain paired until Catalog-horizon expiry, so sequential churn cannot reuse capacity hidden behind a lower concurrent-request count or terminal request.

Before durable Configuration publication, Core pauses ordinary reservations and creates one Prepared Carry Reservation in the Catalog-proved dedicated nonborrowable slot. It binds the predecessor and successor Budget identities and Support Start Count Bounds, current Support Ledger Generation, every Catalog-retained active charge, operation obligation, physical credit, entitlement vector and retained tombstone, every lifecycle reserve, the Catalog Retention Horizon, and the maximum separately typed dual-Budget mandatory-completion and safety capacity for bounded drain-through-activation work. Covered records remain conservatively retained while the token is live rather than expiring underneath its proof. Every later mandatory or safety reservation must consume prepared capacity while satisfying both Budgets and both count-bound tables; it advances the ledger only through the token's registered suballocation edge, so the proof remains closed. Any unrelated ledger mutation invalidates the token. Immediately before mutation-owner creation, the Event Loop atomically revalidates the complete mutation token, exact carry token, current Support Ledger Generation, current next assignable value, and complete headroom. Every nonfatal mismatch closes the unowned carry, resumes ordinary support, and returns without an Operation ID or owner. At Control Publication Commit Barrier entry the Event Loop revalidates the exact token and a current zero-request-liability witness under the closed Runtime Closure Gate; only that gate's nonincreasing-transition invariant makes the witness stable before Store I/O. Committed Control atomically installs the daemon-qualified successor Budget, count-bound table, and Runtime Overhead Generation with the same Core ledger and consumed records. After owner creation, graceful prepublication cancellation, Fence-attempt exhaustion, and trustworthy exact Store absence each return one typed nonpublication terminal Result to the sole Core outcome transition; that transition consumes the token exactly once, preserves predecessor Budget and charges, releases only unused prospective carry capacity, resumes ordinary reservations, closes the Core owner/headroom, reopens the Runtime Closure Gate, and returns a typed disposition. It never reads or mutates the Event Loop-owned Control Mutation Cancel Gate; daemon persistence orchestration clears that gate immediately after accepting the disposition and releasing the owner in the same Event Loop handling step, with no intervening dequeue or Core transition. Audit Degraded retains the same token and suballocations for exact continuation. A durability-indeterminate path fabricates no Result and fail-stops without in-process release. Committed activation may close unused prospective carry capacity and then expire covered records, credits, and tombstones by Catalog horizon, but no actual charge, timestamp, credit, vector claim, or pool identity is refunded or reset. Mismatch after commit is an invariant failure and process-wide fail-stop rather than partial activation or a fresh window.
_Avoid_: Event Loop-owned counters, tumbling window, configuration-reset budget

**Sequenced Event Interference Bound**:
The finite immutable daemon-owned descriptor for every non-Backend Runtime Event Loop/Core event that may execute ahead of a fresh Scheduling Snapshot while a Timing Commitment remains live. Its exhaustive registry maps each event kind and bounded input bucket to a complete owner-thread envelope from dequeue, Monotonic timestamp and Event Sequence assignment through validation, `Core::handle`, accepted transition, immediate in-memory Effect issuance, and scheduling-disposition update. It excludes work already inside a Turn, support, Residency, Exclusive, or local-stale envelope. At every synchronized scheduling-trigger boundary before the Event Loop forms any fresh Snapshot while a Timing Commitment survives, it fixes a scheduling cut over the already admitted bounded Core Event prefix. This single rule covers the first runnable plan after Admission/materialization or Candidate Formation, Receipt, Plan Rejection, local-stale disposition, any other support Result that can make work runnable, and idle re-entry; none may dequeue an uncut ordinary prefix or form the Snapshot directly. A separate nonborrowable mandatory-crossing allowance limits cancellation, disconnect, Critical, failure, and shutdown events admitted after that cut; once its fixed count is consumed, later signals coalesce or defer behind scheduling, while an event that cannot legally defer invalidates all affected Timing Commitments and enters its bounded fail-stop path. `sequenced_event_interference(H)` is the externally qualified checked maximum for the frozen prefix plus that allowance in horizon `H`, derived from the exact registry, Hot-Path maxima, global Core Event Reserve, and fixed cut rule. No other event admitted after the cut can overtake the fresh Snapshot and selected Turn. Prepared Control results and other ordinary events wait behind the cut. Thus every event that runs while any promise survives is already included once; invalidation is never used retroactively to erase owner-thread time. A measured envelope excess or an unclassified event invalidates Lifecycle Overhead Qualification and fail-stops before another scheduling or Backend call. This static cut-bound interference has no runtime charge ledger and cannot be widened from observations.
_Avoid_: Hot-Path operation count as time evidence, unbounded priority queue, double-counted support work

**Stale Plan Disposition Bound**:
The finite immutable complete daemon-envelope bound for the intrinsic local path from the Event Loop's final pre-call Plan identity check through one accepted Local Stale Plan Core Transition, Audit Effect issuance, and intrinsic fresh-Snapshot/replanning disposition. It ends before any `form_candidates` preparation. The local transition closes the impossible Receipt-branch obligations and only marks the shared rejection/local-stale formation obligation pending or closes it on typed causal impossibility; after the intrinsic envelope ends, a standalone `begin_support` transition may convert that pending obligation for one separately measured Candidate Formation support envelope. It is a companion Runtime Overhead Catalog entry activated only by Lifecycle Overhead Qualification, independent of request Certification Applicability and the stale Plan's now-inapplicable Runtime Overhead Bound Set. Every admitted Set and Timing Commitment freeze its identity, value, allowed intrinsic successor ceiling, and the exact support-interference ceiling that funded that operation path. On mismatch, the Event Loop may submit the local event only when the currently active qualified bound is no greater than that frozen intrinsic ceiling and the operation obligation remains valid; otherwise it fail-stops without a Backend call, fabricated Backend Result, or unbounded Domain Rejection. Measured excess of this bound invalidates the lifecycle qualification and takes the same fail-stop path.
_Avoid_: Backend Plan Rejection bound, stale Set authority, unbounded retry

The remaining five Interface operations have closed classifications: `initialize` is startup work before the support lifecycle, `execute_turn` is classified by its Result, `execute_exclusive` requires shared dispatch paused, `transition_residency` consumes Residency Service, and `shutdown` begins only after the support lifecycle ends. Adding an Interface operation without exactly one lifecycle and timing classification is a build failure; no owner-thread queue is free background work.
_Avoid_: Model Ledger, unbounded maintenance queue, background free work

**Backend Operation Bound Set**:
The bounded versioned build-fixed descriptor returned by Backend Initialization that maps every Backend Interface operation kind and bounded input bucket to its finite maximum continuous blocking bound, next-safe-point bound, cancellation class, and conservative Resource Impact. Before invoking `initialize`, the daemon already has that operation's externally verified entry and the expected complete Set identity from its Backend Bootstrap Manifest; the returned descriptor must match exactly before any later call. Exact Capability Key or Model Descriptor evidence may supply a tighter Turn or Residency bound but may never exceed this Set's applicable maximum. The daemon binds the verified Set identity into the Environment Fingerprint and refuses Service Readiness on mismatch; a Backend claim does not certify itself. The Set supplies per-call inputs to Engine, Residency, Exclusive, and Owner-Thread Support gating through the one Interface and has no hidden dynamic timing side channel.
_Avoid_: Runtime estimate, self-authorization, unbounded callback

**Backend Bootstrap Manifest**:
The immutable build-generated descriptor embedded in the daemon before the Device Executor invokes Backend Initialization. It binds the expected Adapter, dependency, Backend Interface, complete Backend Capability descriptor including its Generation Semantics Identity, Backend Resource Signal Contract, and complete Backend Operation Bound Set identities plus the finite initialization blocking, next-safe-point, cancellation, and Resource Impact entry certified for that exact build. The daemon verifies this static artifact against external conformance and operation evidence before the call, requires its Generation Semantics Identity to equal the daemon Domain Type registry, starts the initialization watchdog from its bound, and requires the returned complete descriptors to match it exactly. It contains no runtime environment fact, Certification Applicability, Admission, or Resource Mode decision and is not a second Backend Interface.
_Avoid_: Backend self-attestation, runtime handshake, hidden side channel

**Hot-Path Work Budget**:
The binary hard maxima for one serving decision or Core Transition, including active Models, eligible requests per Model, Work Candidates, Batch members, Core Events examined, bytes copied, allocations, and invariant work. Admission and ingress reject before accepted state can exceed these maxima, no path silently truncates work, and verification asserts the operation counts in addition to wall-clock latency.
_Avoid_: Performance target, average benchmark, unbounded safety scan

**Deadline Cost Bound**:
The checked conservative maximum `B` of both complete Backend result branches for one Work Candidate attempt, plus one `support_interference(H)` and one `sequenced_event_interference(H)` from the same exact Runtime Overhead Bound Set. The Receipt envelope is pre-call intrinsic Runtime Overhead plus the certified Engine Service upper bound plus Receipt validation, Core commit, and Output Publication overhead. The Plan Rejection envelope is pre-call intrinsic Runtime Overhead plus the complete rejection-call bound, rejection validation and Core commit, and one intrinsic fresh-Snapshot/replanning disposition; it contains zero Engine Service. Its admitted local-disposition ceiling separately covers the active intrinsic Stale Plan Disposition Bound without treating a stale Set as current authority. Both branch envelopes exclude Candidate Formation and every other support envelope already represented by support interference, and exclude every scheduling-cut Core-event envelope already represented by sequenced-event interference. Admission validates every authorized phase, batch, Shape, and result case by proving at least one configured certified horizon satisfies checked `B + support_interference(H) + sequenced_event_interference(H) <= H`, then reserves the maximum resulting value across that complete future-case closure. The support term includes initial Materialization and Candidate Formation, separate Receipt observation and conditional continuation formation calls, the mutually exclusive rejection/local-stale formation path, cancellation membership-change formation, and ownership release required by that future closure. For a later exact Work Candidate, deadline-cost composition selects the smallest such `H` for its exact case; absence makes the Candidate infeasible. Its Deadline Cost Bound is the checked three-term sum, never above the admitted maximum, so an arbitrarily aligned interval covering that attempt cannot receive an uncharged support burst or scheduling-cut event prefix. Latest Safe Start uses this end-to-end maximum rather than Engine Service alone. A rejected Plan ceases to exist, and any replacement candidate recomputes its own bound from the fresh Snapshot after any separately measured Candidate Formation.
_Avoid_: Fairness charge, observed average latency

**Turn Cost Estimate**:
An Execution Backend-provided ordinary estimate for a Work Candidate paired with the immutable certified upper bound referenced by its Capability Key. Turn Receipts may calibrate the ordinary estimate within that bound, while the Scheduler consumes both values without modeling backend operations itself.
_Avoid_: Token count, Scheduler guess, certified Turn boundary

**Cost Profile**:
The versioned online calibration state used by the Execution Backend to produce ordinary Turn Cost Estimates and translate a Turn Plan's time target into a concrete Prefill Chunk, Decode burst, or micro-batch within fixed Certification Record bounds. It may update only inside the compare-and-set `observe_turn_receipt` operation for an already accepted Turn Receipt and only between Turns, so every Scheduling Snapshot observes one immutable version. It cannot create a Backend Capability, widen a certified upper bound, or change Admission safety margins.
_Avoid_: Certification Record, Model Ledger, Timing Profile

**Cost Profile Update**:
The typed compare-and-set result of owner-thread `observe_turn_receipt` for one already accepted Turn Receipt. The Receipt binds the expected current Cost Profile and Backend Generation. A mismatch returns a typed pre-mutation rejection; because Core prevalidates both identities before invoking the call, that unexpected rejection is a divergence fault and fail-stops before another Backend call. A match returns either `unchanged` or atomically installs one new Backend profile and returns `applied` with exact Receipt, affected Model, old-version, and new-version identities. Backend retains the calibration parameters; Core mirrors only the accepted profile identity and Backend Generation. An `applied` result must cross the Cost Profile Commit Barrier and be committed exactly once in the immediately following Core Transition, advancing Backend Generation, invalidating every older Scheduling Snapshot, Turn Plan, and not-yet-admitted Request Description, and marking only that Model dirty so only its cached Work Candidates are reformed. That accepted Core transition may mark the retained shared continuation-formation obligation and its pre-reserved post-observation description set pending or close either on typed proof that it is unnecessary, but it never converts an obligation within the observation envelope. After that envelope ends, a standalone `begin_support` transition must convert each required pending obligation immediately before its Backend call; capacity was already conserved and cannot be borrowed from ordinary support. A malformed result or inability to commit after Backend mutation likewise triggers process-wide fail-stop; the daemon never continues with divergent Core and Backend versions. The update changes only ordinary estimates and never widens a certified upper bound or rewrites the Receipt.
_Avoid_: Turn Receipt, Certification Record, online bound widening

**Cost Profile Commit Barrier**:
The short fail-closed Event Loop boundary beginning when `observe_turn_receipt` atomically applies a Backend profile and ending when its exact `applied` result becomes the next Core Event and Core commits the mirrored profile identity plus Backend Generation. No other Core Transition or Backend call may intervene; inbound events may queue only within their existing bounded ingress capacity. Result mismatch, invariant failure, or inability to commit terminates the process rather than exposing divergent versions.
_Avoid_: General transaction manager, profile ownership transfer, asynchronous calibration queue

**Profile Revalidation**:
Every durable Control successor, not only a Configuration change, performs the one atomic Control-owned Runtime Overhead Generation advance before this process consumes it. The Configuration case below is representative and does not create a narrower or second owner.
The Turn-boundary process triggered by activating a new Certification Record, changing a Backend Capability bound, invalidating a Runtime Overhead Bound Set, activating a new complete Configuration Snapshot, or changing another certified feasibility input. For non-Control evidence invalidation, its sole Core transition advances Runtime Overhead Generation and invalidates older not-started artifacts. Configuration activation instead advances that generation exactly once in the same atomic Control-successor transition, after which Profile Revalidation consumes the already advanced value and cannot advance it again. Both paths invoke the same pure helper to rerun Admission-owned applicability selection and feasibility for existing Resource Reservations. Revalidation never rewrites the frozen obligation or original evidence in a Timing Commitment; it installs only a current derived feasibility witness from a newly applicable Bound Set. If the conservative current bound no longer fits the frozen obligation, Core emits SLO Risk and blocks related new Admission rather than using stale evidence, online widening, or unbounded urgency. An ordinary Cost Profile estimate update within unchanged certified bounds does not trigger it.
_Avoid_: Automatic bound expansion, new-request-only update

**Bound Violation**:
A completed Turn or control operation whose actual time or resource use exceeds its Certification Record upper bound. A Prefill Turn that consumes beyond its granted chunk or fails to return synchronized continuation by that bound is the same violation; an internal full-prompt or multi-chunk loop cannot redefine the Turn. Its Receipt remains authoritative, but the most specific affected Capability Key is removed from shared scheduling, an auditable contract violation is emitted, and re-entry requires explicit recertification. Correlated failures may escalate quarantine to a wider Envelope, Adapter build, or Backend Capability. A resource-bound violation also forces immediate Resource Governor reevaluation; a bounded root-recovery underestimate follows Repository Root Recovery Bounded Recovery Capacity Admission Boundary Bound Violation and its Affected Operation Boundary, quarantining the exact recovery Tool/Capability and allowing only already externalized operations to reach their pre-reserved safe terminals. Exceeding only the ordinary Cost Profile estimate is normal calibration evidence, not a Bound Violation.
_Avoid_: Ordinary estimate error, automatic bound expansion

**Backend Capability**:
A versioned Execution Backend claim authorized by one or more Certification Records that a class of work satisfies specific execution, synchronization, resource, cancellation, and output bounds within a named Certification Envelope. Its complete descriptor binds the exact Generation Semantics Identity and has a content identity fixed in the Backend Bootstrap Manifest and checked against Backend Initialization; the Backend cannot supply its own expected value. The MVP shared-execution contract declares `max_overlapping_turns = 1` and authorizes Cooperative Turn Interleaving with exactly one Backend Turn in flight; this limit is an explicit capability, not an accidental property of the Device Executor Implementation. Individually valid Capability Keys never imply simultaneous multi-stream safety. Any future concurrent-stream mode requires a separate architecture decision and correctness, attribution, latency, throughput, and peak-memory certification for the complete co-running set. A capability is never universal across Apple Silicon, model revisions, Adapter or MLX builds, Backend Interface revisions, OS versions, memory sizes, or generation semantics. A quarantined Capability Key cannot form shared Work Candidates until recertified.
_Avoid_: Work Kind, Backend process, model support

**Attention Path**:
The exact Adapter-internal attention execution plan composed with one KV/cache layout for one Turn.
